description: All identified contradictions across Trinity convergence — conflicting claims, sources, and their possible resolutions

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: CreatorOS has authentication (login/registration pages, session management, Passport.js integration)
CLAIM B: comparePasswords() returns true for ALL passwords — authentication provides zero security
possible_resolutions: R1: Auth UI exists but is non-functional as a security boundary. Both claims are true simultaneously — the code has auth 'structure' but no auth 'function'.
R2: comparePasswords may be a development stub that was never replaced with a real implementation.
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — treat auth as completely broken. The presence of login pages does not mean security exists. Plan full Clerk replacement.
contradictions.rationale: A function that returns true for all passwords is equivalent to no authentication. The UI exists but provides false sense of security.
blocked_actions_until_resolved: Cannot deploy CreatorOS to any public URL

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: OS Platform Standard v1 recommends Firebase auth
CLAIM B: Clerk is the target auth direction for all Trinity apps
possible_resolutions: R1: OS Platform Standard v1 Firebase recommendation is stale and replaced by Clerk in v2
R2: Firebase was a temporary recommendation that was never implemented
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — Firebase auth recommendation is STALE. v2 replaces it with Clerk. Do not canonize Firebase.
contradictions.rationale: No Trinity app actually uses Firebase auth. The recommendation was never followed. Clerk is the active direction.
blocked_actions_until_resolved: Do not reference v1 Firebase recommendation as current

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: GitHub main is the authoritative source (202 files, Replit Agent authored)
CLAIM B: Beast feature/company-system is the active development branch (603 files, Clerk, company system)
possible_resolutions: R1: Promote Beast to main — it is 3x larger and represents months of active development
R2: Cherry-pick Beast features into GitHub main — keep GitHub as the base
R3: Keep both — defer decision
R4: Discard Beast — restart from GitHub main
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — Promote Beast to main after validation (build, secret scan, test).
contradictions.rationale: Beast is the active codebase. GitHub main is stale. Promoting Beast aligns source truth with development reality.
contradictions.confidence: HIGH for recommendation, LOW for execution (needs validation)

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: PRD v1 defines the product scope
CLAIM B: PRD v2 exists with potentially different/expanded scope
possible_resolutions: R1: PRD v2 supersedes v1 — use v2 as canonical
R2: PRD v1 is the MVP scope, v2 is the roadmap
R3: Both are valid — v1 for current MVP, v2 for future direction
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — PRD v2 as canonical, since the deployed MVP likely reflects v2 thinking.
contradictions.rationale: Version 2 of a PRD typically reflects refined product thinking. The deployed MVP at lyfeos.net likely incorporates v2 features.
contradictions.confidence: MEDIUM — need to verify PRD v2 content against deployed MVP
blocked_actions_until_resolved: Feature scope decisions for LyfeOS expansion

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: Google Docs contain the desired product/end-state truth
CLAIM B: Code on Beast/GitHub contains the current implementation reality
possible_resolutions: R1: Docs = desired, Code = current. These are different dimensions, not contradictions.
R2: Where code is AHEAD of docs (Beast has features docs don't mention), both are partial truths.
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — maintain the distinction. Docs = intent, Code = reality. When code is ahead of docs, the code reveals implemented intent that docs haven't caught up to. When docs are ahead of code, docs reveal desired features not yet built.
contradictions.rationale: This is the core source truth model. Neither supersedes the other. Both are inputs to the production design.

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: Beast branch has Clerk auth already integrated and working
CLAIM B: Beast branch has never been CI-validated or build-tested
possible_resolutions: R1: Clerk exists in code but is unvalidated. Both claims are true. 'Integrated' ≠ 'validated'.
R2: Clerk may work locally on Beast but fail in other environments.
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — Clerk is present in Beast code but not validated. Do not treat as 'working' until build validation passes.
contradictions.rationale: Code presence is not proof of functionality. Validation is required before claiming auth works.

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: LyfeOS is deployed as an isolated MVP at lyfeos.net
CLAIM B: UMH-connected MVP is the desired end state
possible_resolutions: R1: Both are valid stages. Isolated MVP = current. UMH-connected MVP = future.
R2: 'Isolated' means not connected to UMH substrate. The app works independently.
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R1 — isolated MVP is the current state. UMH-connected MVP is a future phase. Both are valid. The isolated MVP proves the product works. UMH connection adds orchestration, intelligence, and cross-app capabilities.
contradictions.rationale: Sequential maturity stages, not contradictions. Current → future.

conflicting_claims: CLAIM A: CreatorOS PRD describes a comprehensive creator platform (content, courses, community, distribution, analytics)
CLAIM B: Current codebase is a Replit-origin scaffold with god files and broken auth
source_refs: Phase 14.4 inventories and desired state canons
possible_resolutions: R1: PRD is the vision, code is the starting point. Large gap between them.
R2: PRD scope may be too ambitious for the current codebase quality.
R3: MVP scope (DEC-145-002) bridges the gap by defining a realistic subset.
contradictions.recommended_resolution: R3 — use MVP scope decision to define what is buildable given the current codebase quality. Full PRD scope is the long-term vision, not the immediate target.
contradictions.rationale: Attempting full PRD scope on a codebase with broken auth and god files is unrealistic. Staged approach via MVP scope decision.

summary.note: Most contradictions are resolved by maintaining the docs-vs-code distinction or by recognizing sequential maturity stages. The truly blocking contradiction is EOS source divergence (CONTRA-003), which requires operator decision DEC-145-001.
